disease_label_per_paper: Severe combined diabetic ketoacidosis and lactic acidosis
presentation_summary: 22-year-old man with insulin-dependent diabetes was found unconscious and brought by helicopter emergency medical service.

Prehospital exam showed marked Kussmaul breathing, sinus tachycardia 117/min, blood pressure 67/30 mmHg, Glasgow Coma Scale 1-1-1, dilated unreactive pupils, and a tonic-clonic seizure during examination.
The article states there was no evidence of systemic infection on physical examination.
First ED arterial blood gas showed plasma glucose 59.0 mmol/L, pH 6.57, PCO2 3.3 kPa, bicarbonate 2.0 mmol/L, lactate 13.3 mmol/L, sodium 149 mmol/L, and potassium 3.9 mmol/L.
Admission labs also showed WBC 41.6 x 10^9/L, CRP 1 mg/L, urea 12.5 mmol/L, and creatinine 165 micromol/L.

outcome.source_text_value: Metabolic derangements normalised within 36 h, after which the patient could be extubated making a full neurological recovery.

quality_warnings: The paper diagnosis and treatment response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
No ketone value was reported in the extracted presentation text, so no ketone axis was invented.
Severe lactate elevation and shock are preserved as rankable presentation evidence rather than treated as exclusionary mimic evidence.
